Working Relationship  
Ursula and I collaborated on a few SaaS projects at NexaCorp, primarily focused on scaling backend systems. As a peer, I observed her consistently prioritize reliability and efficiency, often stepping in to debug complex microservices or optimize database queries. Her approach to problem-solving felt intuitive—she’d dissect systems with a methodical curiosity, rarely needing direction.  

Day-to-Day Observations  
Ursula’s daily work revolved around maintaining and extending microservices, with a particular focus on PostgreSQL performance. She’d spend hours refining queries or redesigning data models to handle growing user loads, often sharing insights that improved team-wide practices. Her REST API designs were clean and pragmatic, balancing simplicity with scalability. While I didn’t manage Kubernetes, I saw her troubleshoot pod scaling issues during peak traffic, ensuring services stayed responsive. AWS was her go-to for infrastructure, and she’d often explain choices in terms of cost vs. reliability, which helped align the team.  

Standout Moments  
During a critical outage, Ursula rebuilt a failing API endpoint using Go, reducing latency by over 40% without external dependencies. She also spearheaded a PostgreSQL migration to a sharded architecture, which stabilized our database under heavy load. Her ability to balance deep technical knowledge with clear communication made her a natural leader in ad-hoc troubleshooting sessions.  

Recommendation  
Ursula’s strength lies in her ability to translate abstract system challenges into concrete, maintainable solutions. She’s reliable, proactive, and has a knack for making complex systems feel manageable. Her work ethic and technical depth make her a strong fit for any team needing robust, scalable backend expertise.
